speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin)  : Achieving arts excellence in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In recent years, the Government, arts companies and enterprises have been working together to organise many arts and cultural activities for people of different ages and background.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I think that beyond introducing and promoting arts, we should work towards achieving arts excellence.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Besides growing our local arts audience and arts lovers, we need to groom more top-notch arts professionals, so that the entire arts scene can be more vibrant and diversified!

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts play an important role in defining our national cultural identity.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Growing the local arts audience is one of the priorities in the National Arts Council's (NAC's) SG Arts Plan.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: From Independence to now, our arts and culture scene has been developing very fast, and arts promotion has also achieved marked results.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In our schools, besides knowledge and skills, allowing students to access arts through art classes is part of our holistic education to fully develop their character.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts can stimulate curiosity and creativity in our students.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For students who are more talented, we need to provide them with a more professional training platform so that, one day, they can become one of the world’s top artists.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In order to groom our own local artists and talents, we should develop and have our own arts university.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This will enable the arts students to further their arts study at the tertiary level in Singapore and be recognised.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Next, while promoting arts, we should constantly seek new heights.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: How can we groom future professional artists for our flagship national arts groups?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For these arts professionals, we need to provide them with a more flexible learning framework and environment, and a specialised career path.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: After graduation, they will be able to work at our national arts flagship companies.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: With a steady supply of professional artists, arts managers and researchers, our local arts ecosystem will be greatly improved.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Their talents were developed and recognised at international arts scenes.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore has the ability to groom these arts talents, and we need to create more such future award winners.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The Government, the Ministry of Education (MOE), the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), schools and arts groups need to attach importance to developing the ecosystem for arts excellence.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: While urging more Singaporeans to attend arts activities, we should also rethink and explore how we can develop arts excellence.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We should not only let arts be down-to-earth but also let Singapore artists and art works shine at the international stage!

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: It has been heartening to observe agencies from different sectors across the Government, arts and cultural companies and enterprises coming together to introduce a series of arts and culture programmes for Singaporeans of all ages.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: As we focus on creating access and opportunities to arts of different forms and also engaging in a deeper and more sustained appreciation of arts, I believe that we should all come together to achieve artistic excellence that inspires.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The arts have always played an important role in defining our nation’s cultural identity in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The arts scene has been thriving as artists chart professional careers and arts groups grow in strength.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: And the SG Arts plan maps the NAC's priorities over the next five years to bring Singapore’s arts development to new heights.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Our arts community has also achieved significant success with distinctive works that have resonated with audiences both locally and overseas.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: And these local talents are our nation’s pride and define our nation's distinctive identity.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In schools, our students are exposed to arts programmes as part of their holistic education.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Be it music lessons or aesthetics lessons, these are part of a student's curriculum.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Also, the NAC's Arts Education Programme provides all students with access to quality arts education experiences.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In terms of co-curricular activities (CCAs), students can choose the Arts CCAs, where they have opportunities to take part in the Singapore Youth Festival (SYF) Presentation as well as the annual SYF Celebrations.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In 2012, the SYF Central Judging was rebranded as a SYF Arts Presentation.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The award structure revamp was put in place by MOE to emphasise enjoyment of the arts rather than the pursuit of awards.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This has provided access and opportunity, increasing the participation rates in performing arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For students who are more talented and seek deeper engagement in arts, there is the Artist-In-School Scheme.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This scheme supports sustained partnerships between Singapore Arts Professionals, such as musicians, dancers and writers, to co-develop customised arts experiences that deepen students' engagement in and through the arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The arts can play a significant role in culture-building, community life and city planning.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: As society becomes more diverse, the arts can help deepen understanding and bridge differences across communities.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that artistic excellence and creating access and opportunities to arts for the masses are two different tracks.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: One, explore the possibilities of transforming our arts academies into a full-fledged Arts University.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The arts must energise and excite Singaporeans, bring people together and reflect what Singapore represents to a global community.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In Our SG Arts Plan, one of our key strategic thrusts was "Singaporeans are empowered to create, present and appreciate excellent art".

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: But where will our creators of excellent art come from?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In pursuit of access and opportunities to arts, we should not forget we ought to reach the pinnacle of excellence.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In order to groom our own local pool of artists and talents, we ought to have reputable arts institutions.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We already have the Yong Siew Toh Conservatory of Music at NUS, founded in 2003; the arts institutions Laselle College of the Arts founded in 1986, NAFA established in 1938, and SOTA founded in 2008.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, as the first pre-tertiary arts school in Singapore, SOTA's programme allows students to take one arts subject, in addition to the usual academic subjects taught in mainstream schools.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: An article then raised questions about the effectiveness of SOTA's programmes in preparing students for a career in the arts.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: As an aspiring Arts Nation, I believe that we should have our own Arts University.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: By transforming or upgrading our arts academies, this will draw local and overseas talents into enrolling into these institutions.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: At present, we do partner prestigious universities overseas, send our students overseas on exchange programmes to broaden their horizon.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Competitive benchmarking is ambitious and it will help one to grow and learn more about their competitors.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Two, establish a robust ecosystem to develop top-notch artists.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans can be proud of our artists and arts groups winning international awards and being featured at leading arts venues and festivals around the world.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that there is a need to redefine our arts ecosystem, so as to provide a greater platform for professional artistes, artistic directors and arts managers.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We do have many top-notch artists, Cultural Medallion and Young Artist Award recipients.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Another 14 of their alumni have been presented the Young Artist Award.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Also, many of their alumni have gone on to make their mark in the professional arts scene in Singapore and abroad.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Lasalle, too, has her fair share of Cultural Medallion recipients.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps we could recognise our Cultural Medallion recipients more during National Arts events, and work closely with the different National Arts Flagship Companies to groom and identify younger talents, then pass on the knowledge from one generation to the next.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Many of them started their music journey since young.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: They were nurtured by dedicated teachers and supportive parents.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We will need to establish a robust ecosystem to develop top-notch artists and management, who are equipped with strategic and critical thinking to groom and nurture the next generation of artists.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In achieving excellence, clear career pathways, programmes and platforms need to be in place, also leading them to join national arts flagship companies.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, young Singaporeans in the arts scenes and future international award winners.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, we do already have young talented individuals in the arts scenes.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Wong Kah Chun was the first Asian to win the prestigious international Gustav Mahler Conducting Competition in 2016.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Violinist Kam Ning has gone on to perform all over the world, both as soloist and chamber musician.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: She was the Second Prize winner at the Queen Elizabeth Competition in 2001.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Fifteen-year-old Chen XinYu was admitted into the NAFA School of Young Talents at the age of six.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: When she turned eight years old, XinYu won nearly all the First Prizes in the National Chinese Music Competition organised by NAC.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: All these are our young Singaporeans, and we should continue to track their performances in the local and international arts scenes.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: These young budding talents are the future of our arts scenes, and we will need more of them.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: What does the future hold for international arts winners in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: To cultivate full-time artists and retain them, we need to have a clear career pathway, leading them into a national arts flagship company after graduation.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We will need the Government, such as MOE, MCCY, NAC, the universities, colleges and art groups to strengthen their core and emphasis on the importance of outstanding artistic development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and NAC work closely with partner agencies and the arts community to develop a rich and vibrant arts landscape in Singapore, including through arts excellence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Terence Ho spoke about the important role the arts play in building our national identity, bringing different communities together and presenting Singapore to the world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY recognises that the arts play an important and critical role in building a caring, cohesive and confident Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are committed to partnering the community to nurture arts excellence even as we grow broad-based engagement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will address Mr Terence Ho’s three suggestions in turn.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: First, I agree with Mr Ho on the importance of providing opportunities for our children to experience the arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Exposure to the arts at a young age can nurture creative thinking and help our children develop empathy and confidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition to the initiatives already highlighted by Mr Ho, NAC has worked to enable quality arts experiences during different life stages from preschool to tertiary education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To give one example, The Artground at Goodman Arts Centre is an incubator space that offers arts programmes for children as young as a few months old, such as the recent programme called "Baby Space" held in April.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC has also collaborated with partners like the Early Childhood Development Agency and the National Trades Union Congress' My First Skool to bring our artists to preschools to enrich their first encounters with the arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Terence Ho asked about the diverse pathways beyond arts practice that have been taken by students from SOTA after graduation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our objective in establishing SOTA more than 10 years ago as a premier arts school to nurture leaders in all fields remains relevant today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SOTA was set up to provide a learning environment where both the artistic and academic potential of our students can be realised, and where a culture of experimentation and expression allows them to discover their passions and their strengths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SOTA has attracted some of our best and brightest students who are capable of succeeding in many fields of study and of gaining entry to some of the top academic institutions in the world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: A SOTA education develops the skills and confidence for students to follow the pathways they wish to pursue in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SOTA's success is not defined only by the number who progress to higher-level arts institutions and become future art practitioners and leaders of arts and culture institutions, but also those who go on to take up other non-arts disciplines, and who then infuse their creative bent and skills into diverse professional fields and industries, such as engineering and law.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These graduates of SOTA are the future patrons, supporters and audiences who champion the arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They are offered at all five polytechnics, Lasalle College of the Arts, NAFA, NUS, including the Yong Siew Toh Conservatory of Music, the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and Singapore Institute of Technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With the competing manpower needs of our economy, it is also the responsibility of the Government to ensure that arts education is competitive in quality and relevance with other disciplines in enhancing the employability of our students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will now turn to Mr Terence Ho's second recommendation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We agree that it is important to establish a robust ecosystem that contributes to the development of artists who can make Singapore and Singaporeans proud.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To achieve this, NAC's Our SG Arts Plan has identified eight priority areas which range from using digital technology to maximising the impact of the arts on society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are also committed to providing sector-wide support for our freelancers to look after their own financial and healthcare needs over the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With their range of skills and expertise, freelancers make an important contribution and should have access to resources that will better equip themselves for the nature of their work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Another priority in the Arts Plan is to grow our audiences, who are critical to a thriving and sustainable arts ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The success of a sustainable arts ecosystem is determined not just by the quality of artists and their works, but also by whether they succeed in connecting with and growing their audiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will, on its part, also step up efforts to help our homegrown talents grow audiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: An example of how NAC has partnered the community to build our audiences is the Hear65 initiative launched in April 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This was done in collaboration with independent music media company Bandwagon to celebrate and promote all forms of Singapore music.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our arts ecosystem is made up not only of artists but also other arts practitioners, such as managers and administrators, educators, researchers and academics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will continue to support the development of arts professionals in all these areas through its initiatives and funding schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, Jean Hair was awarded an NAC scholarship in 2018 to pursue a Master of Arts and Cultural Management and has since returned to Singapore to continue her work at the National Gallery of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are also proud of our 2011 Young Artist Award recipient Joshua Tan, who was appointed Associate Conductor of the Singapore Symphony Orchestra in the same year and went on to be the Principal Conductor of the Singapore National Youth Orchestra.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There are multiple platforms for young artists to showcase and develop their talent, such as the annual SHINE festival organised by the National Youth Council and the Noise Music Mentorship programme by NAC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some who perform well at such events and competitions are engaged by our national companies, such as Moses Gay, a prize winner at the National Chinese Music Competition in the early 2000s, who is now a colleague of Mr Terence Ho as an Assistant Conductor with the Singapore Chinese Orchestra (SCO).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These allow our artists to learn from others, build their markets overseas and share what Singapore is capable of.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY and NAC are committed to developing our young talent and are constantly exploring new ways of doing so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We look forward to his continued partnership and contributions to the development of a vibrant and sustainable arts landscape in Singapore.
